title: Application startup, frame loop and shutdown
summary: Recovered the 922-byte stdcall application entry at VA 0x005CFC90 as readable C++ with live global slots and explicit external dependencies. Direct immutable-EXE disassembly and accepted assembly establish four WinMain arguments (previous-instance ignored), mutex early exit, frequency setup, ignored COM HRESULT, guarded initialization, command transformation, startup checks, virtual calls, frame polling and ordered event shutdown. Caller in CRT startup passes image base 0x400000, null previous instance, command tail and show mode. String capacities, object offsets, global reloads and return values are preserved. Source uses a semantic dependency adapter rather than claiming a directly bound original ABI for unresolved register-only helpers. No matching-source credit.
test_description: Local freestanding GCC i386 build with the specified flags passes eight direct original differential cases: ERROR_ALREADY_EXISTS versus errors 0, 5 and UINT_MAX, each with null/non-null mutex results; all non-183 cases take QueryPerformanceFrequency failure. Compares returns, exact OS call order and arguments, stored handle (including retained closed handle), frequency write and untouched portable state. Original entry and cookie-check accepted assembly were locally linked at their original VAs and byte-compared to Game.exe: all 922 and 15 bytes equal. Local linker maps test dependency data sections .oracle_iat=0x92D000, .oracle_cookie=0xBAABC0, .oracle_frequency=0xC00B48 and .oracle_mutex=0xC0D610. Another 336 C++-only dependency-spy cases cover stage/startup/graphics/worker failure, successful startup, service allocation failure, cached service present, once guard, inline/heap/empty command strings, wide string cleanup, all four loop termination locations, WAIT_FAILED still executing a frame, ordered signals/join/shutdown, command pointer assignment and untouched graphics bytes/worker fields. Full expected call sequences asserted independently. GCC C++11 O2 warnings-as-errors compilation also passes. Ordinary links without the fixed dependency mappings explicitly print LIMIT and run portable assertions only; they do not execute an invalid oracle call.
known_limits: Only the two early-return paths were directly compared with original machine code. Later startup, error-dialog and main-loop paths are instruction-derived and tested with C++ spies, not direct original differential execution.

Original helper 0x008F92EF uses ECX/EDX signed-int64 input and XMM0 result, and calls 0x008F925E for general values. Neither is an accepted reference in this task. convertFrequency remains an explicit dependency; special rounding modes and full-range conversion have not been differentially validated.

The remaining startup graph and virtual methods, including 0x00452D30, 0x00415B00, 0x00560310, 0x00510F30, 0x004A0480 and 0x004A08E0, remain external dependencies. The original caller-pop register ABIs of 0x005C2740 and 0x0044F490 require explicit semantic adapters; no false function-pointer ABI casts were introduced for them.

applicationEntry is a port adapter taking explicit State and Dependencies, not a drop-in four-argument WinMain export. Object and field names are descriptive; layouts model only fields this routine accesses and require a 32-bit target. Linux platform/service implementations are outside the assigned scope.

Original security-cookie machinery and stack-alignment code are compiler/runtime concerns rather than modeled application operations. The original check is used by local early-path tests; security-cookie failure, invalid pointers, exceptions and concurrent mutation are not tested.

Original worker command is a borrowed pointer that remains stored after local command destruction. No artificial clearing, mutex release, handle close on later exits or COM uninitialization was added.
The trusted linker must map the four documented writable dependency sections to run direct oracle tests; an unconfigured link explicitly reports portable-only testing.
Pinned MSVC helper is absent from /tools/msvc in this sandbox. Implementation uses C++11-compatible syntax and guarded calling-convention macros; native Windows compilation was not available locally.
